title: Java Core, Memory Model & Modern Concurrency

units.title: Java Memory Model & Concurrency Primitives
units.description: Core memory visibility guarantees, synchronizers, lock-free patterns, and modern Project Loom virtual threads.

notes.title: Memory Visibility, Reordering & The Happens-Before Guarantee
Virtual Threads & Structured Concurrency

questions.prompt: Which architectural guarantee is provided by declaring a field volatile in Java?
options: Atomic read-modify-write operations such as incrementing (state++)
Visibility of writes to all threads and memory ordering via happens-before relationships
Mutual exclusion locking identical to a synchronized method
Pinning the thread execution to a single hardware core
questions.explanation: Volatile guarantees memory visibility and establishes a happens-before relationship that prevents compiler and CPU memory reordering. However, it does NOT guarantee atomicity for compound operations like state++.

questions.prompt: Which guarantees does entering and exiting an intrinsic synchronized block provide in standard Java?
options: Mutual exclusion ensuring only one thread executes the protected block at a time
Visibility of all variable modifications made prior to releasing the lock
Asynchronous non-blocking execution using carrier threads
Happens-before order between lock release and subsequent lock acquisition
questions.explanation: An intrinsic synchronized block provides mutual exclusion, visibility (flushing writes upon exit and invalidating stale caches upon entry), and a happens-before relationship between the monitor release and any subsequent acquisition.

questions.prompt: Order the sequence of actions when a virtual thread performs a blocking socket read:
items: Virtual thread initiates read() on a network socket channel
JVM intercepts blocking operation and unmounts virtual thread from carrier thread
OS kernel performs network I/O while carrier thread runs other runnable tasks
Kernel signals I/O completion and JVM remounts virtual thread onto an available carrier
questions.explanation: When a virtual thread blocks on non-pinned I/O, the JVM unmounts its execution context from the carrier thread, lets the carrier run other tasks, and remounts the virtual thread upon I/O readiness.

questions.prompt: Match each java.util.concurrent utility to its synchronization characteristic:

pairs.right: One-shot countdown barrier that cannot be reset
Reusable synchronization point that trips when all parties arrive
Maintains a fixed set of permits for rate limiting or throttling
Flexible barrier supporting dynamic number of parties across multi-phase tasks

questions.explanation: CountDownLatch is non-reusable and decrements to zero; CyclicBarrier resets automatically after tripping; Semaphore manages permit counters; Phaser provides phased synchronization with dynamic party counts.

questions.prompt: In Java, to prevent a thread from using stale cached values of a field without using synchronized, you must declare the field with the ___ keyword.
questions.explanation: The volatile keyword ensures direct reads and writes to main memory, preventing thread-local caching in CPU registers or L1/L2 caches.

questions.prompt: Explain the mechanism and trade-offs of Compare-And-Swap (CAS) in atomic classes like AtomicInteger.
questions.modelAnswer: Compare-And-Swap (CAS) is an atomic CPU instruction (e.g. cmpxchg) that updates memory only if its current value matches an expected value. It enables optimistic, lock-free concurrency avoiding thread context switching overhead, but can suffer from busy-wait CPU spinning under high write contention and the ABA problem if not counter-stamped.
keyPoints: Atomic CPU instruction comparing expected vs current value before updating
Lock-free and avoids thread suspension or context switch overhead
Spinning under high contention can consume excessive CPU
Vulnerable to the ABA problem unless versioned (e.g. AtomicStampedReference)
questions.explanation: CAS provides non-blocking thread safety via hardware-supported atomic primitives, trading thread sleep/wake overhead for potential CPU spin cycles under high contention.

questions.prompt: Which condition in Java 21 causes a virtual thread to become 'pinned' to its carrier platform thread during blocking operations?
options: Executing a blocking call inside a synchronized block or method, or calling native code (JNI)
Allocating objects on the heap exceeding 64 kilobytes
Using ReentrantLock.lock() prior to the blocking call
Running the application with more than 8 available CPU cores
questions.explanation: In Java 21, executing blocking I/O while inside a synchronized monitor or foreign/native JNI call pins the virtual thread to its underlying OS carrier thread, preventing the carrier from servicing other virtual threads. Using ReentrantLock avoids this limitation.
